The refactoring is complete and behavior is fully preserved. The created-owner response body is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-refactor baseline (`customerCode: TOW-SUR-0001`, `checkDigit: 8`, `locality: NSW`, `membershipNumber: TOW-SUR-0001-M26`, `householdId: null`), and the only failing test is the pending change's own acceptance test — failing for the exact same reason as before (its regex expects the not-yet-implemented `<REGION>-<HASH8>` format).

## What I did

The three flagged methods are the *post-change* anchor points. I prepared the surrounding code so the redesign lands as a localized, natural edit — without implementing it.

**1. Extracted the SHA-256 hex primitive** (`OwnerRestControllerV1`)
`householdId` had the digest→hex→truncate→upper-case loop inlined. I lifted it into a shared `sha256HexPrefix(source, length)` helper and rewrote `householdId` to call it (`"HH-" + sha256HexPrefix(..., 12)`). This is behavior-identical, and it means the pending `HASH8` (first 8 upper-case hex of SHA-256) becomes a one-line `sha256HexPrefix(normalizedTelephone + lastName, 8)` call instead of a second copy of the crypto boilerplate — which is exactly the duplication the naive `sha256Hex8` anchor represented.

**2. Reshaped the customer-code builder** (`OwnerRestControllerV1`)
Renamed `nextCustomerCode(city, lastName)` → `customerCode(Owner owner)` and moved the field reads inside. The body still produces the current `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` sequence code, so behavior is unchanged — but the method now receives the whole owner, giving the redesign direct access to the postcode (for `REGION`) and the already-normalized telephone (for `HASH8`) it will need. `addOwner`'s call site collapses to `customerCode(owner)`, so the change lands entirely inside this one method rather than inflating `addOwner`.

**3. Left `OwnerMapper::locality` as-is** (deliberately)
It already delegates cleanly to `cityRegionResolver.regionFor(city, postcode)`, and the controller injects that same resolver — so the region source of truth is already centralized. `membershipNumber`, `checkDigit`, and the audit line already consume `customerCode`, so they'll pick up the new identity automatically. Any edit to `locality` now would either duplicate logic or bake in the new format, so the honest prep is none.

The values built from the customer code (`membershipNumber`, `checkDigit`, the audit record) all already read it, so they inherit the new identity for free once `customerCode(owner)` is rewritten.
